issues.description: Identity seed/increment grammar permits sign on both numbers without documenting which TSQL actually allows.
issues.detail: The grammar now accepts an optional SignedSegmentGrammar before both seed and increment NumericLiteralSegments. TSQL's IDENTITY(seed, increment) does allow negative values for both, so this is correct, but the change deserves a one-line comment recording the invariant ("seed and increment may each be signed; both default unsigned") so a future reader does not have to re-derive it from MS docs.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no test fixture exercising that branch.
issues.detail: The OneOf adds NumericLiteralSegment as a permitted form for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, but the added create_login.sql fixture only covers the NakedIdentifierSegment case (us_english). A grammar branch with no test is an unaudited claim; add a CREATE LOGIN ... DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=1033 case so the branch is actually exercised and the YAML hash pins it.

issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor from Delimited(OneOf(...)) to bare OneOf silently narrows accepted syntax.
issues.detail: The previous grammar allowed comma-delimited sequences of alter-actions at the top level (the removed fixture exercised ADD ... , DROP COLUMN ..., DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS ...). The new grammar only allows a single action per ALTER TABLE, pushing Delimited inside DROP COLUMN and DROP CONSTRAINT. This is closer to MS docs but is a behavior change; a one-line comment stating the invariant ("one action per ALTER TABLE; multi-drop handled inside") would help the next reader.

issues.description: TableIndexSegment added to DECLARE table-var body without a corresponding fixture in the diff excerpt.
issues.detail: The single-line addition Ref("TableIndexSegment") inside DeclareStatementSegment is the headline feature for "table var w index" but the visible diff shows no .sql fixture covering DECLARE @t TABLE (... INDEX ix ...). If a fixture exists outside the truncated diff, fine; if not, the grammar change is untested and should not merge without a literate example pinning the parse tree.

issues.description: Nested Sequence(Sequence(...optional=True), ...) inside DROP CONSTRAINT is readable but worth a comment.
issues.detail: The DROP CONSTRAINT branch wraps an optional inner Sequence("CONSTRAINT", IfExistsGrammar) inside the outer Delimited Sequence, which makes the "CONSTRAINT" keyword itself optional. That matches TSQL (DROP CONSTRAINT foo vs DROP foo is not actually legal), so the optional=True may over-accept. Verify with a negative test or tighten by removing optional.

review.summary: This is a parser-only TSQL grammar PR with matching fixtures and regenerated YAML hashes. The algorithmic content is grammar composition (OneOf/Sequence/Delimited), so the rigor lens reduces to: does each accepted branch have a test, and is each refactor's invariant statable in one line. The ALTER TABLE refactor from Delimited(OneOf) to OneOf with inner Delimited is a deliberate behavior narrowing (removed fixture confirms) and is reasonable but unannotated. The identity-sign and DEFAULT_DATABASE/LANGUAGE relaxations are correct per MS docs but underdocumented; DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric and table-var INDEX branches appear under-tested in the visible diff. Decision label: UNDER-AUDITED / NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT — correct in spirit, but the invariants and a couple of grammar branches should be pinned by comment or fixture before merge.
